Japanese officers initially dismissed Americans as spoiled and soft, dependent on firepower. But by late 1943, firsthand combat at Guadalcanal and the Philippines revealed a terrifying truth: American industrial capacity was endless. Sunk ships returned faster than Japan could replace losses. Fresh troops kept coming. One Japanese soldier wrote: "It's like fighting the tide." Fear of American inevitability had begun. #simplehistory
